standard_prerequisites.name: The kernels whose vanishing is regularity
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Defined in the counted proof at lines 16923-16927
standard_prerequisites.use: Encode the regularity of the sequence as the vanishing of finitely many kernels of multiplication.

standard_prerequisites.name: A finite module vanishing after localisation vanishes after inverting one element
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at the last two lines of the counted proof (lines 16928-16930)
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the vanishing of the localised kernels at the given prime into vanishing after inverting some g outside that prime.

core_obligations: Define the kernels K_i of multiplication by x_i on the quotient of M by the previous elements, whose vanishing for all i is exactly regularity of the sequence (proof lines 16923-16927).

Use the assumption that the localised sequence is regular to see each K_i localised at the prime is zero, and use finiteness and Noetherianity to find a single g outside the prime with all K_i inverted at g equal to zero (proof lines 16928-16930).
Conclude that the images of the x_i in R_g form an M_g-regular sequence (proof lines 16929-16930).
proof_roadmap: Codify regularity as vanishing of the successive kernels of multiplication (proof lines 16922-16927).
Localise, then use finiteness to choose one g killing all the kernels at once (proof lines 16928-16931).
difficulty_reason: For a Noetherian ring R, a finite module M and a sequence x_1, ..., x_r whose image in R_p forms an M_p-regular sequence, the lemma produces a single g outside p such that the images in R_g form an M_g-regular sequence (statement lines 16912-16920). The proof does not argue about the localised quotients one by one: it defines the kernels K_i of multiplication by x_i on M modulo the previous elements, notes that each is a finite module vanishing at p by hypothesis, and uses finiteness to choose a common g killing all of them (proof lines 16922-16931). Packing the regularity into finitely many modules, so that one element can be chosen for all of them, is the substance of the argument. H2.
